text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Danish feta-style cheese exports have declined in recent years to only one fifth of 1991-92's record 1.2 billion crowns due not to Denmark's opposition to Tehran's mullah regime over the Salman Rushdie fatwa affair but because Danish exporters are owed 841 million crowns by Iran and calling for tighter export guarantees.

--- Danish Health Minister Yvonne Herloev Andersen wants to stop supermarket sales of alcohol to youngsters under the age of 18. Youngsters' access to alcohol at these outlets is unlimited at present and needs tight control, she says.

--- Denmark is set to lose its position as the EU member state with the lowest inflation and is heading for a bottom listing with an expected 1997 rate of 2.4 percent, according to a new European Commission forecast.

--- Danish exports to Poland increased by 21.8 percent in 1996's first eight months to almost 2.9 billion crowns, with Danish investment in the country continuing to grow and Denmark placing one third of all its eastern European investment there.
